Rashmi: i keep refreshing her mock test score. shes 3 marks ahead 😔
Yash: for the quiz team place?
Rashmi: yes. i cant sleep. i cant think about anything except beating her
Rashmi: i studied 1 hour today. i spent 3 checking her
Yash: thats not studying rash
Rashmi: i hate her
Yash: i think you hate being behind. not the same thing. what would you do if you had nobody to watch?
Rashmi: finish the chemistry chapters

qa.q: What time was it when Rashmi messaged Yash?
What is Rashmi feeling about the other girl, and how does it affect Rashmi's studying?
qa.a: Rashmi feels resentful and anxious about being behind, saying "i hate her" and unable to sleep; Rashmi spent 3 hours checking scores and only 1 hour studying.

qa.q: What would help Rashmi tonight and tomorrow?
qa.a: Rashmi could sleep first and then spend the time on the chemistry chapters instead of checking the other girl's scores.

qa.q: How does Yash see Rashmi's message?

grounding: A teen fixates on defeating a rival, losing sleep and study time, and recognises the obsession drains energy from the teen's own growth.

passage: There was one district scholarship seat for their kasba school, and everyone knew it was between Jeevan and Zeenat. Jeevan couldn't stop thinking about her. He checked her test marks before his own, lay awake counting how many sums she'd done, and on the bus he watched her revise instead of revising himself. One afternoon he found her physics notebook left on a bench and held it a second too long, imagining it gone. His hands felt dirty. He put it back on her desk. That night he couldn't sleep again, and his mock-test score dropped by twelve marks. His grandfather, mending a net on the veranda, said, "You're running her race, not yours." Jeevan turned his desk to face the wall and made a timetable with no Zeenat in it.

qa.q: By how many marks did Jeevan's mock-test score drop?
qa.a: His mock-test score dropped by twelve marks.

qa.q: What was Jeevan feeling when he held Zeenat's notebook a second too long?
qa.a: Jeevan felt a pull of jealousy and then shame, as if his hands were dirty for even imagining it gone.

qa.q: What change helped Jeevan get back to his own growth?
qa.a: Turning his desk to the wall and making a timetable with no Zeenat in it put his energy into his own study.

qa.q: How might Zeenat feel if she knew how closely Jeevan watched her?
qa.a: Zeenat might feel uneasy and pressured, since she is simply revising for the same seat.

grounding: Illustrates a teen fixated on defeating a rival, losing sleep and marks, and recognising the obsession drains his own growth.

passage: Leila had watched every one of Nkechi's netball clips from last season, pausing on her footwork until 1 a.m. The Birmingham under-16 team had one spot for goal attack, and Nkechi was her only real rival. Leila started noticing everything: who Nkechi sat with, what she ate, whether the coach smiled at her. She even drafted a message to the team group hinting that Nkechi had skipped fitness tests, then deleted it, ashamed. At Thursday's practice Leila dropped three easy passes because her eyes were on Nkechi instead of the ball. On the bus home her friend Grace said, "You play against her more than you play the game." Leila stared at the rain on the window. That night she switched off the clips and slept for nine hours.

qa.q: How many easy passes did Leila drop on Thursday?
What was Leila feeling when she deleted the message about Nkechi?
qa.a: Leila felt ashamed, recognising that her fixation was pushing her toward sabotage.

qa.q: What small step did Leila take to break the fixation?
qa.a: She switched off Nkechi's clips and slept, putting her energy back into her own game and rest.

qa.q: How might Nkechi see Leila's constant watching at practice?
qa.a: Nkechi might feel uncomfortable and watched, without knowing why Leila seems so tense around her.

grounding: Shows a teen obsessed with beating a rival, close to spreading a rumour, who sees the fixation is draining her own focus.
